title.rendered: The Name That Is Above Every Name: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: God gave Jesus the name that is above every name, that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow. Every knee. Every name. When the believer speaks in that name, every other name has to answer.

content.rendered:
God exalted Him to the highest place and gave Him the name that is above every name, that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, in heaven and on earth and under the earth. Every knee. Every name. When the believer speaks in that name, every other name has to answer.

The Gospel For Today | Thursday, July 16, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“Therefore God exalted him to the highest place and gave him the name that is above every name, that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, in heaven and on earth and under the earth, and every tongue acknowledge that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.”
Philippians 2:9-11 (NIV)

Today’s Message

Philippians 2 contains one of the earliest and most theologically dense hymns in the New Testament. Paul is describing what Jesus accomplished through the incarnation, the cross, and the resurrection. And when he arrives at the exaltation, he uses the strongest language available in the Greek language to describe the name Jesus now bears. The name above every name. The name at which every knee must bow. The name every tongue will confess as Lord to the glory of God the Father.

This is not sentimental worship language. It is a legal claim about how the universe is now ordered. There is a name in existence, at this moment, that stands above every other name that has ever been named. Every political name. Every corporate name. Every demonic name. Every angelic name. Every ancestral name. Every household name. Every disease name. Every diagnosis name. Every situation name. Every one of them is subject to the name of Jesus. There is no exception clause. There is no rival throne. There is a name above every name, and that name is the name of the One who was crucified, buried, raised, and now sits at the right hand of the Father.

The implications for the believer are enormous. When the believer prays in the name of Jesus, they are not adding a religious tag to the end of their words. They are speaking in the authority of the name that stands over every other name. When the believer commands sickness to leave in the name of Jesus, the sickness is being spoken to by a name it has no legal authority to defy. When the believer breaks a generational pattern in the name of Jesus, the pattern is being addressed by a name that has universal jurisdiction over every claim any other name has ever made. The name is not decoration. The name is authority.

This is why the New Testament writers keep telling the church to do everything in the name of the Lord Jesus. Colossians 3:17: whatever you do, in word or in deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus. John 14:13: whatever you ask in My name, that will I do. Acts 3:6: in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, walk. The New Testament is saturated with the recognition that the believer’s authority is exercised in and through the name of Jesus.

For Gospelbuzz readers, the truth this morning is unshakable. Every situation in front of you today has a name. And there is a name above every name. When you speak in the name of Jesus, you are not making a request. You are declaring the standing order of the universe. Every other name has to answer. Walk in that today.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that You have given Jesus the name that is above every name. Every knee must bow. Every tongue must confess. Every other name in my life today is subject to His name. The sickness has a name and Jesus is above it. The fear has a name and Jesus is above it. The situation has a name and Jesus is above it. I speak in that name today. I command in that name. I pray in that name. I walk in the authority of the name that has universal jurisdiction. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

The name of Jesus is above every other name. Every knee must bow. Every tongue must confess. I speak, pray, and walk in that name today.
